data.name: Mukhthar
data.gender_notes: Mukhthar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mukhthar is a name derived from the Arabic root 'k-h-th-r', which means 'to crush, grind, or pulverize'. In Islamic context, this name symbolizes the triumph of faith over difficulties, and the ability to break down obstacles and challenges. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is an excellent example of this trait, as he overcame numerous adversities to spread the message of Islam.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that inspires strength and determination, reminding the bearer of their ability to overcome challenges and obstacles with faith and perseverance.
data.etymology: Mukhthar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pulverizer, Crusher, Grinder.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mukhthar total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: مختار
in_arabic.meaning: المختار يعني الشخص المختار أو المفضل
in_arabic.long_meaning: المختار هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و يعني الشخص المختار أو المفضل، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قوله تعالى: 'وَيُخْتَارُ مَنْ يُشَاءُ وَمَا يَشَاءُ' (الآية 74 من سورة آل عمران). و يعتبر هذا الاسم من الأسماء ذات المعنى الجميل و الروحاني العميق.

in_urdu.name: مختار
in_urdu.meaning: مختار کا مطلب ہے منتخب شدہ یا پسندیدہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: مختار ایک عربی मूल کا مذکر نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے منتخب شدہ یا پسندیدہ۔ یہ نام قرآن مجید میں بھی آیا ہے، جیسے کہ سورہ آل عمران میں: 'وَيُخْتَارُ مَنْ يُشَاءُ وَمَا يَشَاءُ' (آل عمران 74)۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقالید میں بہت اہمیت رکھتا ہے اور اکثر اس کا انتخاب والدین اپنے بچوں کے لئے کرتے ہیں۔

in_hindi.name: मुख्तार
in_hindi.meaning: मुख्तार का अर्थ है चयनित या पसंदीदा
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुख्तार एक अरबी मूल का पुल्लिंग नाम है जिसका अर्थ है चयनित या पसंदीदा। यह नाम कुरआन में भी आया है, जैसे कि सूरा آل عمران में: 'وَيُخْتَارُ مَنْ يُشَاءُ وَمَا يَشَاءُ' (आल عمران 74)। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत महत्व रखता है और अक्सर माता-पिता अपने बच्चों के लिए इस नाम का चयन करते हैं।

in_pashto.name: مختار
in_pashto.meaning: مختار د منتخب شوي یا غوره شوي مطلب دی
in_pashto.long_meaning: مختار د عربي اصلي مذکر نوم دی چې د منتخب شوي یا غوره شوي مطلب دی. دا نوم په قرآن کريم کې هم راغلی دی، لکه د آل عمران سوره کې: 'وَيُخْتَارُ مَنْ يُشَاءُ وَمَا يَشَاءُ' (آل عمران 74). دا نوم په افغان او پښتون دود کې ډیر اهمیت لري او ډیری وختونه مور او پلار خپلو ماشومانو لپاره دا نوم غوره کوي.

in_english.name: Mukhthar
in_english.long_meaning: Mukhthar is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning 'chosen' or 'preferred'. It is derived from the Arabic root 'kh-y-r' which connotes selection or choice. The name appears in the Quran, for instance, in Surah Al Imran: 'And He chooses whom He wills and what He wills' (3:74). Historically, Mukhthar holds significance in Islamic tradition as a name that reflects divine selection or preference. It symbolizes a person who is specially chosen by God. The name Mukhthar is used across various Muslim cultures and is valued for its spiritual connotations.

historical_references.reference:
Mukhtar ibn Abi Ubayd al-Thaqafi was a prominent leader in the Second Fitna (civil war) in Medina, which occurred from 652 to 656 CE, after the death of Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab. He was appointed leader by a group of Ansar and Khorasani soldiers who were unhappy with Caliph Umar's successor, Uthman ibn Affan, and believed that Mukhtar would lead them to victory in their struggle for power.
Context: Mukhtar led a successful rebellion against Uthman and, after his death, declared himself caliph. He was eventually defeated and killed by the forces of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the rightful caliph, in 656 CE.

Mukhtar al-Khawlani (also known as Mukhtar ibn Abi Sabra) was a prominent leader in the third civil war in Syria, which occurred from 680 to 683 CE, during the Umayyad Caliphate. He was a prominent Syrian Arab leader who opposed the rule of the Umayyad Caliph Marwan I and led a rebellion against him.
Context: Mukhtar was able to capture Damascus in 680 CE and declared himself caliph, but was eventually defeated and killed by the Umayyad forces led by Marwan I in 683 CE.
